name: Conecto
tagline: A hosted chat product: conversations in a browser, with an AI assistant sitting in the thread.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Chat UIs are the most cloned software on earth, and an agent will happily hand you a working one in an afternoon: threads, streaming replies, message history, a key in .env. What it will not hand you is the part that makes a chat product feel alive, which is realtime sync that survives flaky networks, push notifications that arrive when the tab is closed, and a mobile client anyone else will tolerate. If Conecto's value for you is a private assistant with saved conversations, the DIY build is genuinely fine. If the value is other humans being reachable in it, the build is a demo and the product is the thing people actually open. Public detail on this one is thin, so treat the confidence here as low and check the feature list yourself before you start typing.
coreLoopDIY: Self-hosted web chat with persistent threads, streaming model replies over your own API key, and search across old conversations.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic)
Node 20 and a place to run it, a small VPS or a laptop
Basic willingness to run your own database file
whatYouLose: Native mobile apps and push notifications that fire when the browser is closed
Realtime multi-participant sync with presence, typing state, and offline reconnection that actually works
Someone else paying the uptime and model bills, and monitoring them at 3am
Whatever integrations it ships with, each of which is its own OAuth weekend
Polish: file handling, retries, rate limit backoff, and the hundred small states a chat app has
moatNotes: If it is a solo assistant, there is no moat worth the name. If other people are in the thread, the moat is them.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because chat is deceptively expensive to run well. The demo takes an afternoon and the last 10 percent takes months: message ordering under reconnects, notifications that are neither missing nor duplicated, attachments, and a mobile experience that does not feel like a bookmarked webpage. Paying a few dollars a month to skip all of that is a rational trade for most people, and it stays rational as long as the product keeps working while you ignore it.
notes: A weekend gets you a very good private chat app and a very bad shared one.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted personal AI chat app in an empty folder. No accounts system beyond a single shared password, no telemetry, no analytics, no cloud services other than the LLM API.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/chat.db, schema created on first boot.
- Model calls to the Anthropic Messages API using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from .env.local. Streaming responses.
- Runs with: npm install, npm run dev. No Docker required.

In scope:
- Sidebar list of conversations with auto-generated titles from the first user message.
- Chat view: message bubbles, markdown rendering with code blocks and copy buttons, token-by-token streaming via a server route returning a ReadableStream.
- Persist every message with role, content, model, created_at. Resume any conversation on reload.
- Editable system prompt per conversation, stored with the conversation.
- Full-text search across all messages using SQLite FTS5, results link to the message.
- Delete and rename conversations. Export a conversation as markdown.
- Single-password gate: middleware checks a cookie set by a /login page comparing against APP_PASSWORD in .env.local. Nothing fancier.
- Graceful handling of API errors and rate limits: show the error in the thread, allow retry of the last turn.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Multi-user accounts, invites, roles, or presence.
- Push notifications, service workers, or a mobile app.
- File uploads, image generation, tool calling, or RAG.
- Payments, onboarding flows, or email.

Deliverables: working app, .env.example listing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and APP_PASSWORD, and a README with setup in under ten lines. Commit nothing secret.
